Hours (line 20), he is buried along with the past ages darkened by his reign, and the hours of those ages
here grieve for him (lines 15–20). The identification with Olympian Zeus imports into the figure of
Jupiter an association with time, the sky and the calendar. Cp. II iv 32–3 and note.

paragraphs.source_en:
Haste, oh haste!
 As shades are chased,
Trembling, by day, from heaven’s blue waste,
We melt away,
25 Like dissolving spray,
From the children of a diviner day,
With the lullaby
Of winds that die
On the bosom of their own harmony.
